transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Blake (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (BrightBridge CTO), Samir Gupta (BrightBridge ML Eng), Alicia Park (PM), Rajeev Menon (Infra)

Summary (auto): agree on model lock for pilot, validate circuit-breaker fallback, run benchmarks

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give a quick status then dive into model selection and the circuit breaker scenarios. Connor and I are here from Redwood. Uh, how's everyon—
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Good, thanks. We got the perf spreadsheet you sent, skimmed it, Samir had some initial q's about p95 numbers.
[00:27] Samir Gupta: Yeah, those p95 numbers look good for the smaller quantized candidate but curious about tail when we hit 100 QPS with longer context.
[00:36] Connor Blake: Right, so we ran a stress with 100 QPS, seq=128 and seq=256. For seq=256 the 95th jumped up, we added continuous batching but the KV cache thrash is visible. (note: "K-V cash" in raw logs sometimes spikes)
[00:50] Alicia Park: Quick ask—our SLA target is 120ms p95 for user-facing chat, is that still realistic?
[00:57] Connor Blake: Short answer: with the recommended quantized variant and prefix caching we're in the 90–110ms ballpark at 50–60 QPS, 100 QPS is closer to 130–180 at p95 depending on prompt shape. There's a gap to close.
[01:14] Lena Ortiz: Hmm, that's above target. What are our tuning levers again?
[01:19] Maya Patel: We have three levers: 1) model choice (bigger model vs distilled/quantized), 2) batching strategy and batch size caps, and 3) routing—soft-routing to cheaper variant under load or an emergency hosted fallback.
[01:32] Rajeev Menon: For security, any fallback needs to be VPC-friendly or reside in our private deployment. We can't have PHI routed to a third-party hosted endpoint, so the fallback must be a private-compatible variant or routing must strip PHI.
[01:45] Samir Gupta: Can Redwood host a private fallback that meets our KMS/HSM policies?
[01:50] Maya Patel: Yes, with Redwood Private we can deploy into your VPC or provide air-gapped on-prem package. KMS integrations are supported; we'll share the SOC2 and Architecture whitepaper after the call.
[02:02] Connor Blake: Regarding model variants, we compared three options in the catalog: 1) BB-Large-70B (baseline quality), 2) RB-Quant-13B (quantized candidate), 3) RB-Tiny-6B (emergency fallback). Our eval shows RB-Quant-13B is the best cost/latency compromise but you lose ~3–4% on key accuracy metrics vs the 70B.
[02:23] Alicia Park: That 3–4% is within our threshold as long as the eval set aligns with production prompts. We'll send the 500 prompt set today.
[02:31] Maya Patel: Perfect. On version locking: we recommend a two-week lockpoint for the pilot where you pin to the RB-Quant-13B hash v2026-05-10 and enable soft-fallbacks. Soft-fallback means requests try quantized first, then after N retries or latency > threshold, route to RB-Tiny-6B or fall back to a pre-warmed hosted endpoint depending on policy.
[02:53] Samir Gupta: How do we detect the circuit breaker—based on queue length or token latency?
[02:58] Connor Blake: We usually combine signals: sustained p95 > 150ms for 3 minutes, or queue depth > X (configurable), or GPU utilization > 90% for two consecutive collection windows. Then circuit breaker trips and routes to the emergency path.
[03:15] Lena Ortiz: If it routes to RB-Tiny-6B, quality will degrade. Is there a graceful degradation plan? Our UX team wants explicit messaging when quality is degraded.
[03:25] Maya Patel: Yes—two things: 1) you can surface a confidence banner in the UI (we can emit a quality_score header per response), 2) automatic rate-limited retries to the primary model post-cooldown so we don't keep hammering the primary pool.
[03:38] Rajeev Menon: Also need audit logs for every routed request for compliance.
[03:42] Connor Blake: Absolutely—request-level routing metadata and audit events are supported; we'll provide the log schema.
[03:49] [Brief crosstalk as someone drops a file]
[04:02] Samir Gupta: On the eval side, we ran A/B on 200 prompts; RB-Quant-13B passed the intent-preservation threshold on 188/200 but had higher hallucination score on financial data subset.
[04:18] Sophia (Speaker 7 mistakenly labeled): Sorry, mislabel, that's Samir speaking.
[04:22] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll prioritize the financial prompt subset for targeted tuning. Connor, can we run targeted calibration with prompt templates?
[04:30] Connor Blake: Yes, we'll include prompt engineering suggestions — e.g., more explicit system instructions + retrieval augmentation to reduce hallucinations.
[04:38] Alicia Park: Can retrieval add latency? We worry about adding external retrieval calls.
[04:43] Connor Blake: Retrieval will add some latency; that's why we recommend caching and local retrieval stores in the VPC to reduce RTT. For the pilot, we can test with a small vector DB inside your VPC.
[04:56] Lena Ortiz: Ok, so concretely what's our lockpoint decision now?
[05:00] Samir Gupta: I'm leaning to lock to RB-Quant-13B (v2026-05-10) for the two-week sprint, with an emergency fallback to RB-Tiny-6B but only for non-PHI routes. For PHI we need private fallback or no fallback.
[05:13] Maya Patel: That's reasonable. We should also add a soft threshold where low-confidence responses get routed to a human-in-loop path.
[05:20] Rajeev Menon: HIL is OK, but we need the latency SLA for human review flows documented.
[05:26] Maya Patel: We'll document expected human review SLAs as part of the playbook.
[05:30] Connor Blake: On the benchmarking plan: I'll run the 100 QPS suite with seq lengths [128, 256], collect p50/p95/p99 and token-level cost. I'll export a heatmap and the raw logs. We'll annotate the runs with kernel selection and quantization flags.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: Which metrics should we look at to decide we can cut over?
[05:49] Connor Blake: Primary: p95 latency under 120ms at our expected QPS; Secondary: error rate <0.5% and hallucination aggregate metric per eval < threshold. Also cost per 1M tokens within your cap.
[05:59] Samir Gupta: For rollback—if we see a regression post-cutover, what is the escape hatch?
[06:04] Maya Patel: We have three escape hatches: 1) immediate version rollback to previous hash (instant routing config change), 2) shadow traffic rollback then gradual ramp-down, 3) region-level failover to an isolated capacity pool. We'll provide a runbook with commands and expected RTO.
[06:20] Alicia Park: And who has permission to execute those?
[06:24] Maya Patel: We'll coordinate RBAC: AE/SE can trigger rollbacks in the staging plane; production rollbacks require an authorized operations list—usually your infra lead + Redwood SRE contact. We'll put that in the runbook.
[06:38] Rajeev Menon: Need SSO/SAML integration before prod cutover.
[06:42] Maya Patel: Understood — Redwood supports SAML/SCIM; we'll send the config doc.
[06:49] [Longer silence as participants review the shared benchmark spreadsheet]
[07:20] Connor Blake: Note on batching—if you increase max batch size beyond 16 you see better throughput but worse tail. So we usually set adaptive batch caps.
[07:33] Samir Gupta: Ok. For the next run please test both adaptive and fixed batch cap=16.
[07:39] Connor Blake: Will do.
[07:42] Maya Patel: Anything else on fallbacks?
[07:45] Alicia Park: One more thing—can we simulate an emergency trip during the benchmark so we see the actual UX behavior?
[07:50] Connor Blake: Yes we can inject a circuit-breaker event and replay traffic to measure failure modes. I'll include a replay plan in the benchmark doc.
[08:00] Lena Ortiz: Great. Recap then?
[08:03] Maya Patel: Recap: 1) Lock to RB-Quant-13B v2026-05-10 for two weeks; 2) Connor to run 100 QPS throughput runs (seq=128/256), adaptive vs fixed batch cap=16, and inject circuit-breaker test; 3) Samir to provide 500 prompt eval set and acceptance criteria; 4) Redwood to share cost/latency spreadsheet + security docs by 2026-05-18; 5) Schedule canary for 2026-05-25 if metrics pass.
[08:27] Samir Gupta: Sounds good.
[08:30] Maya Patel: Ok we'll follow up with the links and the benchmark sheet. Thanks everyone.
[08:36] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcript: There are a few mislabels and typical ASR artifacts (speaker labels and proper nouns sometimes off). References to KV cache occasionally transcribed as "K-V cash" in the raw logs.
